Lessons.Title: Using Normal Distributions for Experiment Analysis
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Use the results from redistributing data from an experiment into groups to determine whether the original difference in means is significant.

Under a no-treatment-effect model, randomization redistributes response labels or group membership to estimate the chance of an observed or more extreme difference. A fraction of 20 of 1000 simulations as extreme corresponds to estimated p≈0.02, with simulation uncertainty.

Source activity 14.2: A Theoretical Experiment: To see what might be happening when we regroup data, consider an experiment that takes 12 subjects and divides them into 2 groups at random. The control group contains 6 subjects and the treatment group contains 6 subjects. To explore what's possible, assume the control group results in the data: 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The treatment group results in the data: 2, 5, 7, 9, 11,… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
